criteria.description: Correctly computes the gradient of the quadratic attractive potential.
Correctly identifies the negative gradient as matching DYN-02's P control law exactly.

solutions.fullSolution: grad U_att(q) = grad[ (1/2)Kp||q-q*||^2 ] = Kp(q-q*). F_att(q) = -grad U_att(q) = -Kp(q-q*) = Kp(q*-q). This is exactly DYN-02's P control law u=Kp(q*-q): gradient descent on the quadratic attractive potential is P control.

criteria.description: Correctly describes X as the unrestricted embedding space.
Correctly describes X_fea as the joint-limit- and collision-restricted subset.
Correctly identifies that this open chain's coordinates are already minimal.

solutions.fullSolution: X: the generic embedding space for the two joint angles, e.g. R^2, with no restriction applied yet. X_fea: the subset of X actually reachable, i.e. [-pi/2,pi/2]^2 intersected with whatever region avoids the obstacle (a bounded region with a notch/hole cut out). Minimal coordinates: the two joint angles are already minimal (open chain, no holonomic constraint linking them), so n=p=2; joint limits and collision only shrink X_fea within X, they don't change the coordinate count.
